children: Shares of personalized clothing company Stitch Fix
fell 16.2% in the pre-market session after the company issued cautious revenue guidance for fiscal year 2027 and lowered third-quarter expectations following its second-quarter earnings release.

According to a company press release, Stitch Fix reported 6.4% year-over-year full-year revenue growth for the period ended August 1, 2026, while second-quarter revenue rose 4.2% to $324.4 million. The release also said that its fiscal year 2027 revenue outlook reflects a more challenging consumer environment and a lower active client starting point that will temper top-line growth. Stitch Fix also lowered its third-quarter revenue expectations, attributing the reduction to a shift of Fix shipment volume into the second quarter of 2026.

In addition, the company cited an unintended change to its post-checkout offer flow in August that restricted clients eligible to request another Fix. Management further noted that its adjusted EBITDA guidance reflects planned investments in advertising and technology. At the midpoint, third-quarter revenue guidance of $325.5 million fell below analyst estimates of $352.2 million, while full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $34.5 million missed Wall Street projections of $56.53 million.
What Is The Market Telling Us

Stitch Fix’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 47 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Stitch Fix and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 12 months ago when the stock dropped 16.8% on the news that the company reported its second-quarter 2025 financial results, which revealed a drop in revenue and a shrinking active client base.

For its second quarter, the online personal styling service announced that net revenue fell 2.6% from the previous year to $311.2 million. More concerning for investors was the continued decline in its user base, as active clients dropped by 7.9% year-over-year to 2.31 million. This decrease in customers seemed to outweigh the company's positive forecast for the next quarter.

Stitch Fix provided revenue guidance with a midpoint of $335.5 million for the third quarter of 2025, which was well above analyst expectations. Despite the strong outlook and a nearly 6% rise in revenue per active client, the shrinking customer base signaled potential long-term challenges that prompted investor concern.

Stitch Fix is down 57.1% since the beginning of the year, and at $2.20 per share, it is trading 61.1% below its 52-week high of $5.64 from January 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Stitch Fix’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $50.19.
